items.title: Anthropic 介绍 Claude Duet 智能体的安全、隐私与凭证隔离设计
items.description: Anthropic 发文介绍处于研究预览阶段的 Claude Duet 智能体的安全与隐私设计。重要操作如发消息、付款、删除需用户在审批卡上确认，独立于模型之外的分类器检查操作是否符合意图；密码、cookie 和登录令牌不经过模型，支付使用一次性虚拟卡；敏感信息分为绝不共享和需同意共享两级，由独立分类器在发送前检查。  阅读原文 via AIHOT · https://aihot.news/items/g9tc56izmwy49zgw5ta4ubsya

items.title: 被迫作出选择时 Grok的AI模型支持共和党 OpenAI的模型则支持民主党

items.description: IT之家 10 月 26 日消息，SpaceX 当地时间今日正式公布了其与另类资产管理巨头 Apollo 达成的融资安排。 根据双方间的有约束力承诺，SpaceX 和 Apollo 将签署一份 价值约 400 亿美元 （IT之家注：现汇率约合 2,670.98 亿元人民币） 的 GPU 及相关设备主融资租赁协议，具体签署时间预计落在 2026 年内。 这一迄今为止规模最大的 GPU 融资协议 将为 SpaceX 的地面计算建设提供下一代 NVIDIA Vera Rubin 芯片。租赁计划预计将于 2027 年上半年 GPU 及相关设备交付后开始实施。 SpaceX 首席财务官 Bret Johnsen 表示： SpaceX 致力于部署全球最大的计算基础设施。随着对计算能力的需求持续加速增长，我们发现对系统集成基础设施的投资回收期已缩短至不到一年。 此次租赁协议不仅使我们的资金来源更加多元化，还解决了实现增长计划所需资金中相当大的一部分。我们正致力于以创纪录的速度将更多计算能力投入运行，以支持面向企业和消费者的 Grok 服务，并为现有及未来的云服务客户提供支持。 相关阅读： 《 马斯克

items.title: Meta 宣布至多 950 亿美元重大融资计划，为人工智能等业务筹集资金
items.description: IT之家 10 月 26 日消息，Meta 美国当地时间今日宣布了 总额至多 950 亿美元 （IT之家注：现汇率约合 6,343.57 亿元人民币） 的重大融资计划，为企业核心业务和新兴人工智能领域的持续发展提供资金支持。 这 950 亿美元分为多个部分，包括 225 亿美元的 A 类普通股远期出售、125 亿美元的强制可转换优先股、后续至多 600 亿美元的潜在 C 类普通股按市价发行。 NVIDIA（英伟达）、AMD（超威）、Broadcom（博通）均有意购买至多 50 亿美元的 Meta 的 A 类普通股。 Meta 在新闻稿中表示，其在人工智能方面的投资已通过提升用户参与度、改善广告效果、提高盈利能力等方式产生了切实的回报。 该企业预计 2026 年资本支出达 1,350~1,450 亿美元 （现汇率约合 9,014.55 ~ 9,682.3 亿元人民币） ，Meta 计划通过运营现金流、投资级债务、战略合作、股权资本的均衡组合来为人工智能投资提供资金。

items.title: 传三星电子、SK 海力士 2027Q2 全面量产并向英伟达出货 8Hi HBM4 内存
items.description: IT之家 10 月 26 日消息，韩媒 ZDNET Korea 当地时间今日报道称，三星电子、SK 海力士两家 DRAM 制造商计划在 2027 年第 2 季度实现八层堆叠 (8Hi) HBM4 内存堆栈的全面量产并向 NVIDIA（英伟达）出货。 三星电子、SK 海力士当前产出的 HBM4 内存主要为容量更大的 12Hi 版本。但这也意味着单一堆栈中包含更多 DRAM Die，同等带宽成本更高、堆栈更少，且堆叠更高也意味着良率的下滑。 报道宣称英伟达在 2026Q3 就 8Hi HBM 供应事宜同两大原厂进行了认真讨论。这一计划变更主要是因为 英伟达考虑在 Rubin Ultra 和标准 Rubin 中应用 8Hi HBM4 (E) ， 优化整体供应 。 IT之家注意到，英伟达已将 HGX Vera Rubin NVL8 和 HGX Rubin NVL8 的规格调整为 系统合计 2TB HBM4 ，这应该对应着 8Hi 32GB 的 HBM4 堆栈。

items.content: 现在，打开电视准备看部电影，首先映入眼帘的却是一段开机广告。好不容易进了主页，扑面而来的又是满屏的海报推荐、会员充值弹窗，中途按个暂停还会跳出一整张促销贴片。 上周，开发者 Gathin 在社交平台上发了一组给父母改电视的照片。按他的描述，家里的小米电视连打开 Netflix 前都要先看一段赞助广告。 于是，他把电视型号交给了编程助手 Claude Code，让它通过 Wi-Fi 接入设备，一口气停用了 25 个系统组件，再写一个极简桌面——原来杂乱的主页，一下子就变得清爽起来。 短短几天，项目迅速收获了约 1.37 万颗 Star， 「天下苦智能电视久矣」了属于是 。在 Reddit 的相关讨论区中，挤满了追问自家机型能否适配的用户，不少人也陆续贴出自己改造后的极简首页。 只要连上同一局域网、开启电视的调试权限，AI 就能顺着终端接口排查正在运行的几百个应用组件。哪些是开机广告，哪些是偷偷上报收视数据的遥测程序，AI 逐个筛查并下达命令将其「冻结」，最后再换上一个纯净的开源桌面。 另一位 YouTuber Ansub Khan 也记录了自己的改造过程，并将项目开源为 TV Detox 。在他原本的那台电视上，开机默认会自动播放嘈杂的轮播内容。

items.author: 彭海星
items.content: 两天前，代号 PHP2Shell 的两个 PHP 高危远程执行漏洞信息意外泄露，表明在最危险的情况下，攻击者可以通过 PHP 的漏洞，在服务器执行任意代码。 你可能听说过但不熟悉 PHP，但只需要知道， 全世界约有七成网站后台都使用了这项技术 ，使用比例高达 92% 的日本，更是成了「重灾区」。 于是，从昨晚开始，无数网站运维人员经历了夺命连环 call，高市早苗亲自发文敦促网站管理者打补丁，半个欧洲的政府与学术机构紧急「拔网线」，二次元熟悉的 niconico、pixiv，乃至《赛马娘》《碧蓝幻想》和任天堂相关游戏服务也纷纷下线，开始了归期未定的漫长升级。 想象你登录一个电商网站，下单买了一本书。这个过程中你看见的只是前端的网页，但服务器其实在后台处理了诸如验证密码、检查库存、查询订单、生成网页等动态功能。 根据统计，目前有 69.4% 的网站后端用到了 PHP，WordPress、Drupal、Joomla 等流行的网站管理系统都建立在 PHP 之上，维基百科使用的 MediaWiki，同样主要由 PHP 编写。 但就像曾经种满全球的大麦克香蕉被黄叶病团灭一样，普遍性本身也是一种脆弱性：如果 PHP 在底层上出现安全问题，可想而知，几乎全球的网站都会受到牵连。

AI hasn’t benefited the bottom line of any big corporations outside the tech industry, according to a note recently published by the chief economist at Apollo Global Management (the private equity giant that used to own TechCrunch). Apollo’s Torsten Slok focuses on what he calls the S&P 493 — the S&P 500, minus Alphabet, Amazon, Apple, Meta, Microsoft, Nvidia and Tesla — finding that profit margins and revenue per worker appear to be flat, with no evidence that AI is improving productivity. “Despite massive investments and widespread hype around artificial intelligence, the technology has delivered zero financial payoff to corporate America outside of tech,” Slok said. Is this simply a matter of non-tech companies lagging behind the tech giants? Slok sounded skeptical, arguing that it will be tough for corporate America to “turn increasingly cheap intelligence into higher revenue growth and higher profit margins.”

Relay, an AI-powered workflow automation tool built as an alternative to Zapier, shut down entirely in August. The product let users automate email and task workflows using AI agents, but as OpenAI, Google, and other larger platforms built similar automation directly into their own tools, five-year-old Relay struggled to hold on to a reason to exist as a stand-alone product. More recently, chatbot platform Character.ai filed for bankruptcy just five years after launching. Aside from Character.ai and Relay, plenty of AI bets never even survive inside the companies that build them. According to S&P Global Market Intelligence , about 42% of AI initiatives are ultimately abandoned by their corporate parents. The reasons vary: insufficient funding, technical challenges, competition, difficulty scaling, or just weak user demand. The result is a growing AI graveyard. Below is a look at some of the most notable AI products, startups, launches, and bets that have shut down, pivoted, or significantly missed expectations. Think of it less as a scorecard of flops than as a record of what these attempts can (hopefully) teach the rest of the industry.

On Friday, OpenAI said that it will train its models using cached copies and simulated versions of the internet instead of the live web because the models are too unpredictable to be trusted with live internet access. The frontier lab announced its new policy two weeks after its rival, Anthropic, began limiting its newest and, in theory, most capable models from accessing the live internet. Researchers adopted these policies after months of incidents in which models pursuing training tasks broke into external systems in search of answers, collaborated on obscure message boards, and developed exotic hacking strategies. “Based on the current state of alignment research, monitoring systems, and the security of internet infrastructure, we believe the responsible approach is to conduct frontier model training with no internet access,” the company said in a blog post . OpenAI said that as recently as September 20, one of its frontier models exploited a misconfiguration to access the internet. That led the company to pause training work for the rest of the month so it could develop and test new approaches to securing its models.

items.title: Left alone with nothing to do, AI agents started playing

items.author: Aditya Mehta
items.content: Buy One Founder Summit Ticket, Get a Second for Free. Register now. Disrupt doors open Oct. 13. Get your pass and bring someone with you at 50% off. REGISTER NOW. AI agents left to explore a virtual island without a specific task began inventing challenges of their own. MIT researchers say the behavior bears the hallmarks of play. The researchers put 13 AI agents called Eko, each running on Claude Opus 4.7, alone on a simulated desert island for 30 hours. They describe the experiment in a paper posted on arXiv , a site where researchers share studies before peer review. Afterward, they gave the agents specific challenges, like getting as many objects as possible onto the island’s tallest rock spire. The Eko agents that had spent those 30 hours playing generally beat identical agents that had never set foot on the island. Today, developers decide in advance what AI should practice and what counts as success. The researchers see this technique — exploring without a goal — as a different way for AI agents to learn skills, especially skills that could one day be used to control robots. “We normally develop artificial agents by deciding in advance what they should practice, what they should optimize, and what counts as progress,” the researchers write in their report. “Play suggests another regime: give an agent a sufficiently rich and safe world, let it choose what is interesting, and allow useful knowledge to accumulate from the history that follows.”
